The iOS API/workflow can help achieve the same high-level outcome, but only through a materially different object model or multi-step workflow. It is useful for migration design, yet it is not a direct API-level equivalent.
The comparison is use-case based rather than name/signature based: both sides are evaluated on whether they let an iPhone application accomplish the same practical media task.
Differences:
The callback model is different. iOS may use delegates, blocks, Audio Queue/Audio Unit callbacks, notifications, or KVO; callback lifetime, queue/thread delivery, reentrancy, and unregister semantics must follow the Apple framework contract.
AVFoundation separates capture-device format, connection state, preview layer, video-data output, rotation coordination, and session execution. A HarmonyOS output-local property may therefore become device-, connection-, layer-, or session-scoped on iOS; camera permission and runtime format/device capability checks remain relevant.
Availability / preconditions: iOS 4.0+: setSampleBufferDelegate(_:queue:); iOS 2.0+: removeObserver(_:). Use the cited Apple API only on supported iOS versions and validate runtime device/format/session support where the framework requires it.
